description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the minimum final displacement error (minFDE₂₀) and the ratio of training data used for different trajectory prediction models. The x-axis, labeled "Ratio," ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.2, representing the proportion of the dataset used for training. The y-axis, labeled "minFDE₂₀ (←)," spans from 0.8 to 1.3, indicating the minimum final displacement error, with lower values signifying better performance. Four models are compared: TrajICL (blue, solid line with circular markers), Head Tuning (orange, solid line with circular markers), LoRA 16 (red, solid line with circular markers), and LoRA 64 (purple, solid line with circular markers). The TrajICL model consistently achieves the lowest minFDE₂₀ across all ratios, starting at approximately 0.9 and slightly decreasing to around 0.85. Head Tuning starts at a higher error of about 1.3 and decreases to approximately 1.05. LoRA 16 begins at 1.2 and decreases to about 0.92. LoRA 64 starts at 1.22 and decreases to approximately 0.92. All models show a general downward trend in error as the ratio increases, indicating improved performance with more training data.
